properties.areaDesc: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters; Chuuk Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 1 at 12:15PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
The latest forecasts from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) and
numerical guidance continues to strengthen Tropical Storm Choi-Wan
(26W) as it crosses the Marianas sometime this weekend, possibly
stalling or slowing to a crawl as it does so, becoming a typhoon by
the end of the weekend. Choi-Wan is then forecast to turn north and
accelerate somewhat during the early to middle portion of next week
while it continues strengthening, possibly into a major typhoon.

As all of this occurs, the west to southwest monsoon flow already
encompassing northern Palau (mainly near Koror) and western Yap State
will continue strengthening, with sustained winds of 15 to 20 knots
possible. Strong moisture pooling near the trough axis combined with
at least decent surface convergence should foster increasing shower
and thunderstorm coverage and intensity as we head into the weekend
and early next week. Current indications are for 3 to 6 inches of
rainfall, locally in excess of 8 inches being probable for northern
Palau and western Yap State. This could lead to some minor flooding
concerns and landslide potential, especially near Koror where the
steeper terrain is juxtaposed with the strong moisture pooling and
surface convergence.

As the winds increase, and Choi-Wan strengthens, seas and surf will
also increase. This could lead to hazardous conditions for the
northern reefs and potentially for small craft traversing the waters.

Residents across northern Palau and western Yap States are encouraged
to continue to follow forecast trends at www.weather.gov/gum and on
social media.

properties.headline: Tropical Storm Warning issued October 1 at 9:10AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...NEWLY NAMED TROPICAL STORM CHOI-WAN CONTINUES MOVING WEST-
NORTHWEST TOWARDS THE FAR NORTHERN MARIANAS...

.NEW INFORMATION...
Tropical Storm 26W is now named Choi-wan.
A Tropical Storm Warning is now in effect for Tinian and Saipan and
their adjacent waters in the CNMI.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides important information and recommended
actions for people in Guam and the Northern Marianas.

.WATCHES/WARNINGS...
A Tropical Storm Warning is now in effect for Tinian and Saipan in
the CNMI.
A Tropical Storm Warning remains in effect for Alamagan and Pagan in
the CNMI.
A Typhoon Watch remains in effect for Alamagan and Pagan in the CNMI.
A Tropical Storm Watch remains in effect for Agrihan in the CNMI.

A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions, including
winds of 39 to 73 mph, are possible within 48 hours.
A Typhoon Watch means that typhoon conditions, including winds of 74
mph or more, are possible within 48 hours.

A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected within 24 hours.

A Flash Flood Watch remains in effect for Tinian and Saipan. Please
listen closely for any Flash Flood Warnings that might be in effect
for your area.

All persons in the Watch areas should review their preparedness plan
and begin to take actions to prepare for conditions as indicated by
your local forecast and additional details, below, for your island.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 7 AM ChST, the center of Tropical Storm Choi-wan (26W) was located
near latitude 16.3N, longitude 149.5E. This was about 370 miles
east-northeast of Guam. Storm motion was west-northwest, 285 degrees,
at 9 mph. Storm intensity was 40 mph.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Tropical Storm Choi-wan (26W) has increased in forward speed once
again, with a slight expansion in the tropical storm-force wind field
expected to the west and southwest, keeping Tinian and Saipan well
within said wind field. As such, the Tropical Storm Watch was
upgraded to Tropical Storm Warning for Tinian, Saipan and their
adjacent waters. Timing of further intensification and storm trek
remains largely unchanged. Choi-wan will continue west through
tonight, making a turn to the northwest Friday morning as it begins
to approach Alamagan from the south and intensify into a typhoon,
turning sharply northward, to then move north-northeastward late
Friday night. This forecasted passage over Alamagan and Pagan is
still expected to prolong the duration of damaging winds across the
northern islands, likely leading to a lengthy period of time of
damaging to destructive tropical storm conditions beginning this
evening and continuing into Sunday afternoon. As Choi-wan is forecast
to strengthen to a typhoon Friday morning as it approaches Alamagan,
this would bring Alamagan and later Pagan, directly within the
typhoon force winds Friday night through early Saturday morning. So,
a Typhoon Watch and Tropical Storm Warning remain in effect for
Alamagan and Pagan.

It is too early to provide exact wind and surge forecast values for
specific locations. A general concern should be for the possibility
of at least damaging winds likely somewhere within the Northern
Marianas.
properties.instruction:
Stay indoors during heavy rain and tropical storm-force wind conditions
associated with Tropical Storm Choi-wan (26W). Heed the advice of
your local emergency managers and officials, and continues to monitor
forecasts by the National Weather Service office in Tiyan, Guam.
Remain in sturdy shelter until the all-clear is given.

...WIND INFORMATION...
Breezy northwesterlies today will quickly increase toward the late
afternoon, with tropical storm force winds of 35 to 45 mph with gusts
to 60 mph expected beginning tonight, lasting through at least
Saturday as Tropical Storm Choi-Wan (26W) stalls slightly on approach
to the Far Northern Marianas. This is expected to expose Tinian and
Saipan to a longer period of potentially TS conditions. At this time,
strong tropical storm-force winds look to remain north of Saipan and
Tinian as said winds are expected to remain closely packed near the
center of the system.

...COASTAL INUNDATION AND SURF INFORMATION...
Surf will initially build to 8 to 11 feet along north-facing reefs
by tonight, then quickly spread to west-facing reefs as the center of
Choi-wan crosses the far northern CNMI and exposes a western fetch by
early Friday morning. Surf will continue to increase along all reefs
as Choi-wan continues to strengthen. Coastal inundation of 1 to 2
feet, as well as significant coastal erosion, will be possible along

inches.

to 4 inch range are forecast across the watch area. Locally

Wells, La Salle, Live Oak, McMullen and Webb.

creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
